summary: Audited and repaired TRACE-CONSTRAINT-W3.md; six retractions are bannered at the top of that file: compactness of finite-valued maps in measure (false), Proposition 4 with its 20-of-400 label-pair count (withdrawn), 'limits of one-hot need not be one-hot' (false for strong L2), the 3-periodic sector sequence as a weak-limit model (replaced by Rademacher), 'three labels imply |P_p| >= 3' (the palette is per-direction), and the half-wrong licensing claim. A source audit of Compactness.lean and Palettes.lean fixed the quantifiers: IsTrace is norm-closure at radius exactly 1, ae_typicalSampling is a.e.-in-centre, trace_bounds is proved from weak limits. Prop. 0 repairs licensing: the endpoint trace holds at EVERY centre, since the non-typical set is plane-null and the circle is an isometry of angular measure (paper-level, not Lean's a.e. statement). Prop. 1 is the Rademacher counterexample to the abstract compactness substitute. Prop. 2 and its corollary show the trace-limit route to W3 is incapable, not just blocked: in S_1 every trace is one-hot and strong limits of one-hot are one-hot, so no value count of 3 can arise. Prop. A is kept as a conditional complement-triple claim.
verified_results: GRADE [A] Prop. 1 (Rademacher): on Omega = {0,1}^N with product measure, u_k = e_1 on {omega_k = 0} and e_2 otherwise gives ||u_k - u_l||^2_{L2} = 2*P(omega_k != omega_l) = 1 and P(||u_k-u_l|| >= 1) = 1/2 for all k != l, so there is no Cauchy subsequence in L2 or in measure. Checked exactly on the finite model {0,1}^3 for all three pairs. Hence the set of one-hot fields is not compact, and closed-and-bounded in L0 does not give compactness on a nonatomic space; the compactness step used by the retracted Proposition 4 is false.

GRADE [S] Source audit: Typical z = DensityOne {w | c w = c z} z; TypicalSampling c y r = 0 < r and a.e. t, Typical (y + r*direction t) (Compactness.lean 83-86); ae_typicalSampling is a.e.-in-centre at fixed radius (87-96); sampleCode at 255; sampleSet at 259; IsTrace x b := (x,1,b) in closure (sampleSet) at 261, i.e. closure at radius exactly 1 in the norm topology; trace_realization at 262; trace_limit at 289 (traces pass to limits jointly in centre and trace); trace_bounds at 297 proved from weak limits via traceCode_tendsto_iff plus weak_limit_nonneg, weak_limit_le_one, weak_limit_sum; paletteSet and tracePositive_le_palette in Palettes.lean 9-45.

GRADE [P] Prop. 0: for every centre x and a.e. direction e, c(x+e) is in P_x(e). Proof: the non-typical set N is plane-null, e -> x+e is an isometry of the circle with angular measure, so x+e is typical for a.e. e, hence (x,1,sampleCode) is in sampleSet and its code is a trace at x; tracePositive_le_palette then puts its label into the palette. This is the same argument as m10's Lemma 1 and is paper-level: Lean supplies only the a.e.-in-centre form, so the per-centre form must not be cited as machine-checked.

GRADE [P] Prop. 2 and corollary: in S_1 every trace at every centre is one-hot a.e. (two positive coordinates at a direction would put two labels in a singleton palette; sum of coordinates is 1), and a norm limit of one-hot fields is one-hot (coordinates are indicators, limits of indicators are indicators). Therefore the accumulation-limit argument cannot produce |P_p(e)| >= 3 in S_1: the limit is again one-hot. This closes the trace-limit route to W3 specifically, and nothing else.

GRADE [P] Prop. A retained, hypothesis checked: in S_1 at a centre whose transition graph contains a triangle with label set V, the unit circle is a.e. coloured in T = [6]-V, using Lemma 6.2 on the three edges plus Prop. 0 at the prescribed centre. Sharp in m3's k>=7 colouring where T has k-3 = 4 labels. It yields no finiteness, no separation and no excluded label pair.
conjectures: The one genuinely missing object is a compactness/admissibility lemma for the prescribed sequence of trace codes at triangle centres: that sampleCode c x_n 1 has a norm-convergent subsequence when the x_n are triangle centres sharing a label set. Prop. 0 supplies the admissibility half (per-centre circle typicality); Prop. 1 shows the abstract compactness half is false, so any such lemma must use the specific geometry of the label sets and cannot follow from measurability alone.

Even if that compactness were available, the route cannot contradict S_1 (Prop. 2). So the accumulation-limit mechanism is closed independently of the compactness question; what remains for W3 is a non-limit input, most plausibly from the near field (transition supports at scale h) rather than from radius-1 traces.

Prop. A suggests the useful k=3 complement structure is per-centre and three-valued, which is consistent with m10 Theorem 2 (no centre-independent field), so any label-count argument at k=6 has to be centre-dependent and cannot be discretised.
tests_run: python3 supervisor/solve-geometry/checks/onehot_limit.py (single process, ~20 ms, under the 60 s cap) -> rc 0; appends sections [13]-[14] to supervisor_checks.out: Rademacher pairwise distances 1 and 1/2 on the exact {0,1}^3 model for all three pairs, plus the admissibility bookkeeping against the Lean definitions. supervisor_checks.out is now 72 lines.
failed_routes: RETRACTED Proposition 4 and everything downstream of it (excluded label pairs 20 of 400 and 10 of 210): the compactness of finite-valued measurable maps in convergence-in-measure is false (Rademacher).

RETRACTED the 12-sector 3-periodic sequence as a weak-limit countermodel: it has no weak limit and a constant subsequence exists; it only shows the convex hull of one-hot fields contains non-one-hot elements.
RETRACTED the inference 'b_inf takes three values implies |P_p| >= 3': the palette is per-direction, and one-hot at each direction means cardinality 1.

CLOSED (narrowly) the trace-limit route to W3 in S_1: by Prop. 2 the limit object is again one-hot, so no value count >= 3 can arise; this is a statement about that route only, not about every method.
Retired sources NOTE-far-field.md and notes/LEMMA-D-REPAIRED.md were not relied on for any claim in this block; their broad no-go wording is not adopted.
next_step: If a further block is assigned: state the compactness lemma precisely as 'sampleCode c x_n 1 has a norm-convergent subsequence for triangle centres x_n sharing a label set V' and try to prove it from the specific geometry (the circles S(x_n,1) converge to S(p,1) and the label sets are fixed), or else search for a Rademacher-type family of 6-colourings realising oscillation, which would refute the lemma; given Prop. 2, do this only if the intended conclusion is a statement about the codes rather than about |P_p|.
